title: Relative global complete intersection
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c\ge0$ integers and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; let $T=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$, an $R$-algebra. One says that *$T=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection* (over $R$) if every nonempty fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ has dimension $n-c$: for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ whose fibre ring $T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is nonzero, the Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}(T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (homeomorphic to the fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ over $\mathfrak p$) equals $n-c$. A ring map $R\to S$ is a *relative global complete intersection* if there are such $n,c,f_1,\dots,f_c$ with $T$ a relative global complete intersection and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $S\cong T$.
